questions.enonce_markdown: The appropriate definition of citizenship is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizenship is the legal status of a person who is a full member of a state and who, for that reason, enjoys rights and privileges (for example the right to vote) and carries duties (for example paying taxes and obeying the law). Option D is the only one that contains all three elements: rights, privileges and duties. Option A (belonging) is too narrow, option B describes patriotism and option C describes one duty of a citizen, not the definition itself.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: status of belonging to a country.
participation in the development of one's country.
state of being vested with rights, privileges and duties of a country.

questions.enonce_markdown: An individual who manifests love, respect and parental care, belongs to which component of the home?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A home has a physical component (the house, the furniture, the compound, everything that can be seen and touched) and a psychological component (the feelings and relationships that hold the family together: love, respect, care, security and understanding). A person who shows love, respect and parental care belongs to the psychological component. Physical and visible both refer to the material side of the home.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a type of marriage considered unlawful in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Monogamy (one husband, one wife) is the form of marriage recognised by the law. Polygyny (one man with several wives) is allowed where the husband chose that option at the time of the marriage. Polyandry (one woman with several husbands) is not recognised by Cameroonian law and is therefore unlawful. Polygamy is the general word that covers both polygyny and polyandry, so it is not the best answer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A group of people found within a defined geographical area having the same culture, language and history represents...

*Options as printed:* A) an ethnic group.   B) a tribe.   C) a village.   D) a clan.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An ethnic group is a community of people who share a common culture, language and history and who usually live in the same geographical area. A tribe is a very similar idea and is often used as a near-synonym, so the printed options do not separate the two cleanly. A village is only a settlement and a clan is a group of families claiming a common ancestor within an ethnic group. The best answer is an ethnic group.

**Intended answer: A (an ethnic group).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which institution is put in place by the state of Cameroon to protect the family?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Ministry in charge of social affairs looks after vulnerable people and the welfare of families (support for children, people with disabilities, orphans and the needy). The Ministry of Labour deals with workers and social insurance, the Ministry of Youth Affairs with young people and the Ministry of Justice with the courts and prisons. Among the options, social affairs is the one that protects the family.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance

questions.enonce_markdown: On which part of the high way do students trek from home to school?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pedestrians, including pupils walking to school, must use the sidewalk (the footpath at the side of the road) because it is separated from the traffic. The carriageway is for vehicles. A zebra crossing is used only to cross the road, not to walk along it.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An important characteristic of denominational schools is....
questions.corrige_markdown:
Denominational (mission) schools are run by religious bodies, and they are known for putting strong emphasis on discipline and moral and religious education, that is a high moral standard. Recruitment of trained teachers and moderate fees can be true of any school, and a high teacher-student ratio (too many pupils per teacher) is a weakness, not a characteristic quality.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: He draws up time tables, ensures coverage of schemes of work and assists in the administration of a first cycle school. This description best suites the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a Cameroonian secondary school the Vice Principal assists the Principal and is in charge of academic matters: the time table, the schemes of work and the coverage of the syllabus. The Senior Discipline Master looks after discipline, the head of department manages one subject area only and the Chief Librarian runs the library. The description therefore fits the Vice Principal.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following social ills are common within a school milieu EXCEPT ...

*Options as printed:* A) vandalism.   B) examination fraud.   C) theft.   D) drunkenness.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vandalism (destroying school property), examination fraud (cheating) and theft are all frequently reported in schools. Drunkenness is the least common of the four among pupils, since it is more typical of adults, so it is the most likely intended exception. However, all four are social ills that can occur in a school, so the question is not reliable and the answer is only a best guess.

**Intended answer: D (drunkenness).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The supervisory authority of the City Council is the ...

*Options as printed:* A) Governor.   B) Senior Divisional Officer.   C) Government Delegate.   D) Divisional Officer.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Local councils are decentralised bodies: they manage their own affairs but are placed under the supervision (tutelle) of the central State. Which State representative supervises a City Council depends on the type of council and on the law in force (the Governor, the Senior Divisional Officer or the Divisional Officer, acting for the Minister in charge of local authorities, or a Government Delegate in an urban community). The printed key is probably the Government Delegate, but the question does not say which law or council it refers to, so it cannot be marked with certainty.

**Intended answer: C (Government Delegate).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Council revenue is generated mostly from...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A council collects its own money mainly from local taxes, fees (market fees, parking fees, building permits and similar charges), fines and rents. Royalties and foreign grants are occasional or limited sources, and FEICOM (the Special Council Support Fund) is an institution that supports councils with loans and grants, not a local source of revenue. Fees and fines is therefore the best answer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a major reason that influences the citizens to participate in council activities.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizens take part in council activities (meetings, consultations, community projects) mainly so that the development needs of their locality are identified and carried out: water, roads, schools, health centres and markets. Gaining a job is a personal motive, and control of the council and transparency are outcomes of participation, not the main reason that moves citizens to join in.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The introduction of substance into the environment that cause harm to man and other living organisms is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pollution is the introduction into the environment (air, water or soil) of substances that harm human beings and other living things. Infection is the entry of germs into the body, degradation is the general damage to the environment and ozone depletion is the thinning of the ozone layer.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT an effect of environmental damage?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Landslides, desertification and a fall in tourism are all consequences of damage to the environment. Reforestation (planting trees again) is a remedy, a way of repairing the damage, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cameroon ratified the Kyoto Protocol to fight against...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Kyoto Protocol is an international agreement on reducing the emission of greenhouse gases that cause global warming and climate change. Joining it was a way for Cameroon to fight against environmental degradation. Poaching, the protection of natural sites and the creation of forest reserves are not the aim of the protocol (and the last two are not things to fight against).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The second in command at the Regional Governor's office is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Governor of a Region is assisted in his office by a Secretary General, who ranks next to him and co-ordinates the services of the Governor's office. The Chief of Cabinet, the Inspector General and the Chief of Protocol have more specific duties. The Secretary General is therefore the second in command.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the administrative authority who appoints Divisional Officers in Cameroon.

*Options as printed:* A) The Governor   B) The Minister of Territorial Administration   C) The Head of State   D) The Minister of Decentralization
questions.corrige_markdown:
Divisional Officers are administrative authorities of the central State, so they are not elected. They are named by the central government: by a decree of the Head of State, usually on the proposal of the Minister in charge of territorial administration. Because both the Head of State and the Minister of Territorial Administration are linked to the appointment in practice, the printed question has no single safe key; the Governor and the Minister of Decentralization do not appoint Divisional Officers. The answer given is the Head of State.

**Intended answer: C (The Head of State).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose from the list below the various levels at which Cameroon is administratively structured in hierarchical order.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon is divided into Regions (the highest level, ten in number), each Region into Divisions, and each Division into Sub Divisions (the lowest of the three main levels listed). In order from the lowest to the highest the levels are Sub Divisions, Divisions, Regions. Option A leaves out Sub Divisions, option B wrongly puts Districts above Sub Divisions (districts are small units within a Sub Division) and option D puts the Regions in the middle.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A divisional capital that is NOT a regional headquarters is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Yaounde is the headquarters of the Centre Region, Douala of the Littoral Region and Buea of the South West Region. Limbe is the headquarters of Fako Division in the South West, but it is not a regional headquarters, since the region is administered from Buea.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Offering financial or material gifts to people in authority for undeserved favour is called ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Giving money or gifts to someone in authority to obtain an undeserved favour is bribery, which is a form of corruption. Extortion is forcing someone to pay, favouritism is giving unfair preference to friends or relatives and embezzlement is stealing money entrusted to one's care.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A dubious means to succeed in examinations is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A dubious means is a doubtful or dishonest way. Adequate preparation, teaching that follows the syllabus and effective syllabus coverage are honest ways to prepare. Bringing pre-prepared materials (notes, written answers) into the examination hall is cheating, which is examination malpractice.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify from the list below the main cause of drug abuse.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Young people most often begin to use drugs because friends and classmates push or tempt them to do so (peer pressure), and they want to belong to the group. Lack of civic education, pornography and poverty can contribute, but peer pressure is the most direct and most commonly given cause.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Peter hates Anna because she likes to dress according to the Bakoko tradition. This attitude of Peter is a manifestation of ...

*Options as printed:* A) bigotry.   B) tribalism.   C) nepotism.   D) sectionalism.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Peter dislikes Anna because of her ethnic group and its way of dressing, which is tribalism: prejudice against people because of their tribe or ethnic group. Nepotism is favouring relatives, and sectionalism is placing the interest of one section or region above the national interest. Bigotry (strong intolerance towards people who are different) could also be argued, so the question is not fully reliable.

**Intended answer: B (tribalism).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: As a measure to tackle corruption in Cameroon Article 66 of the 1996 constitution requires that...
questions.corrige_markdown:
To help fight corruption, the Constitution requires holders of certain public offices to declare their assets (what they own) so that any unexplained enrichment can be detected. Making budgets public, publishing reports and controlling expenditure are other good-governance practices, but they are not the measure that this article of the Constitution is known for.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: state officials make public their budgets.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which Ministry in Cameroon caters for delinquent children?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Children in conflict with the law and other children in difficulty are looked after (rehabilitation, protection and reintegration) by the Ministry in charge of social affairs. The ministries of Basic Education and Secondary Education run schools, and Youth Affairs deals with young people in general.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are elements of a state EXCEPT ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A state is made up of a population, a defined territory, a government and sovereignty. A state may be multi-ethnic: it does not need all of its people to belong to the same ethnic group (Cameroon itself has many ethnic groups). A common currency is a feature that most states have, while a central government and political sovereignty are essential elements.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the significance of the Coat of Arms?

*Options as printed:* A) Army, War and Sacrifice   B) Unity, Justice and Peace   C) Civic Responsibility   D) Honour, Dignity and Authority
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Coat of Arms is a national symbol. It is generally read as standing for the values on which the nation is built: unity, justice and peace (the scales of justice and the sword are among its features). Army, war and sacrifice, civic responsibility, and honour, dignity and authority are not the usual explanation. The printed wording is not exact, because the symbol is also linked to the national motto, so the question is left to self-assessment.

**Intended answer: B (Unity, Justice and Peace).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following Constitutions in Cameroon came into effect after the Referendum of 20 May 1972?
questions.corrige_markdown:
On 20 May 1972 the people of Cameroon voted in a referendum to replace the federation of 1961 by a unitary state. The new Constitution was therefore the Unitary Constitution, and the country became the United Republic of Cameroon. The Federal Constitution is the one that was replaced, and the Foumban Constitution refers to the federal arrangements agreed in 1961.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The changes in the Legislative Arm of government brought about by the 1996 Constitution are...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The 1996 Constitution made the legislature bicameral: Parliament is composed of two chambers, the National Assembly and the Senate. Option A is wrong because Parliament is the name of the whole legislative body, which includes the Senate, and options B and C use names that do not describe the two chambers.

**Answer: D.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: To which arm of Government does the Prime Minister of Cameroon belong?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Prime Minister is the Head of Government, appointed by the President of the Republic, and he directs the work of the government with the ministers. He therefore belongs to the Executive arm, which carries out the laws. The Legislature makes the laws and the Judiciary interprets them. Bureaucratic is not an arm of government.

**Answer: B.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cameroon, the institution responsible for interpreting laws is the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Judiciary (the courts and judges) interprets the laws and applies them to cases brought before it. The Legislature makes laws, the Senate is one of the chambers of the Legislature and the Executive carries out the laws.

**Answer: C.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: A relationship that exists between the Legislative and the Executive arms of Government in Cameroon is that the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Parliament (the Legislature) discusses and votes bills, and the President of the Republic (the Executive) promulgates them, that is signs them into law. This is a link between the two arms. The Senate does not appoint ministers (the President appoints the Prime Minister and the ministers), the President does not preside over National Assembly debates, and the President is elected by the people, not voted by the National Assembly.

**Answer: D.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: President of the Republic presides over National Assembly deliberations.
National Assembly votes a new President of the Republic.
Parliament votes bills which the President signs into law.

questions.enonce_markdown: Many people consider democracy as the best form of government because...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Democracy means government of the people, by the people and for the people. Citizens take part in decisions, directly or through the representatives they elect, and this is why many people regard it as the best form of government. Rule by a few, the will of administrators, or citizens imposing their opinions are not features of a democracy.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: rulers are elected by fewer people.
it allows all citizens to participate in decisions.
the will of administrators is considered.
citizens impose their opinions on rulers.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the most glaring consequence of election rigging on a nation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
When elections are rigged, citizens lose confidence in the electoral system and believe that their vote does not count. The most direct and visible result is voter apathy, that is a growing lack of interest in voting. Unemployment and poverty have other causes, and conflict between ethnic groups is only a possible, not a usual, consequence.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a credible electoral process?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A credible (believable) election has transparent ballot boxes, free campaigns and enough ballot papers for all voters. Multiple voting (one person voting more than once) is an electoral offence that destroys the credibility of the result, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the full meaning of the initial CFA.
questions.corrige_markdown:
CFA, as in the CFA franc, is the abbreviation of Communauté Financière Africaine (African Financial Community). The currency is used by several African countries that are linked by monetary agreements. The other options (French community, financial company, fruit company) are not what the initials stand for.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following factors does NOT influence the efficiency of labour?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The efficiency of labour (how much a worker produces) depends on his education and training, on good working conditions, and on proper welfare services such as health care and housing allowances. The size of the company does not by itself make a worker more or less efficient.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: High standards of living as a result of a sustained increase in output refers to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth is the increase in the output of goods and services. When this increase is sustained and translates into better living standards for the people (better income, health, education and housing), it is called economic development. Stagnation means no growth and stability means steady prices and conditions.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A major way by which a citizen contributes indirectly in raising revenue for the state is by...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The main source of public revenue is taxation. A citizen contributes to it by paying taxes (for example tax on goods, VAT and customs duties paid through purchases). Buying stamps raises only a small amount, a civil servant is a user of revenue rather than a source of it, and selling treasury bonds is done by the state, not the citizen.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the effect of the non-payment of taxes by businessmen?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Taxes are the main source of money for the government. When businessmen do not pay their taxes, the state has less money, so it cannot build roads, schools, hospitals and other projects. This direct effect is the limited realisation of government projects. The other options are only indirect or unrelated.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Decrease in the number of foreign investors

questions.enonce_markdown: The entitlement acquired by virtue of birth fits the definition of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Human rights belong to every person simply because he or she is born a human being, whatever his or her nationality, sex or religion. Employment rights depend on having a job, civic rights depend on being a citizen and social rights relate to welfare provided by society.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are some forms of Human Rights violation in the world EXCEPT ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Child labour, arbitrary (unlawful) arrest and detention, and torture are violations of human rights. Imprisonment ordered by the courts after a fair trial is a lawful penalty, so it is not in itself a violation, which makes it the exception.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms was established by the Government to ....
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms is a State body whose mission is to protect and promote human rights: it receives complaints, investigates cases, and carries out education and awareness on rights. It does not prosecute, which is the work of the courts, and it is not mainly responsible for paying compensation.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: organize seminars and workshops for violators
Compensate victims of Human Rights violations.

questions.enonce_markdown: The struggle over values, resources and status with the aim of overcoming the opponent describes...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A conflict is a struggle between people or groups over values, resources or status, in which each side tries to overcome its opponent. This is a conflict situation. A strike is only one kind of action in a labour dispute, and quarrelling and aggression describe behaviours, not the whole struggle.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The UN organ that settles disputes and conflicts between states at the international level is the....
questions.corrige_markdown:
The International Court of Justice is the main judicial organ of the United Nations: it settles legal disputes submitted to it by states. The Security Council is responsible for maintaining peace and security and can take action in a crisis, the General Assembly debates world issues and the Economic and Social Council deals with economic and social questions.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
One direct cause of conflict in the school environment is...

*Options as printed:* A) distribution of materials.   B) invigilation of examinations.   C) on-respect of timetables.   D) Increase in student population.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conflict in schools often arises over scarce resources. When teaching materials and other resources are distributed unfairly or are not enough, people compete for them and quarrel. Invigilation and timetables can also cause friction and a rising number of pupils is an indirect factor, so the printed key is uncertain and the question is left to self-assessment.

**Intended answer: A (distribution of materials).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Gender inequality means that...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gender inequality is unequal treatment or opportunity between men and women (or boys and girls) because of their sex: one sex is preferred to the other in education, work, decision making or inheritance. The other options are statements about numbers, strength and intelligence, and the last one is a false stereotype.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: one sex is preferred to the other.
one sex is more populated than the other.
one sex is physically stronger the other.
one sex is less intelligent than the other.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One measure taken by the Cameroon Government to protect minority groups is by....

*Options as printed:* A) appointing them to posts of responsibility.   B) giving them free education at all level.   C) according them free interest loans.   D) awarding them free land certificates.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Constitution commits the State to protect minorities, and one way it does so is by giving members of minority groups a fair place in public life, for example by appointing them to posts of responsibility. Free education at all levels, free loans and free land certificates are not general measures for minorities. The printed question does not name a specific law or policy, so it is left to self-assessment.

**Intended answer: A (appointing them to posts of responsibility).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The state of affairs whereby children are forced to work instead of going to school is known as.....
questions.corrige_markdown:
Child labour is work done by children who are too young to work or that takes them away from school and harms their health and development. Child trafficking is moving children from place to place to exploit them, child abuse is mistreatment in general, and child exploitation is a wider idea.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Other nationals who come to Cameroon because of war in their country are called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave his or her country because of war, violence or persecution and who seeks safety in another country. Immigrants move voluntarily to settle in another country, foreigners is the general word for non-nationals and settlers are people who establish themselves in a new area.

**Answer: C.**
